nodes.name: Hydrophilic treatment of carbon paper
nodes.procedure: Carbon paper (CP) was cut to a specified size and then placed in a water bath in a nitric acid solution at 50°C. The purpose of this step was to increase the oxygen-containing functional groups, such as hydroxyl and carboxyl groups, on the surface of the CP. After washing repeatedly with deionized water and absolute ethanol and drying in a vacuum box after cleaning, hydrophilic carbon paper (H-CP) was finally obtained.

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of NiCoP without magnetic field
nodes.procedure: 2 mmol NiCl₂·6H₂O, 2 mmol CoCl₂·6H₂O, 5 mmol NH₄Cl, and 5 mmol NaH₂PO₂·H₂O were dissolved in 50 mL of deionized water and stirred uniformly for 30 min with a magnetic stirrer to form an electrodeposition solution. H-CP was used as the working electrode, a platinum sheet as the counter electrode, and a saturated calomel electrode as the reference electrode to construct a three-electrode system. The cell was then placed in a magnetic field of 0 mT at a specified temperature. The deposition parameter was maintained at a constant potential of -1 V for 30 min. After the electrodeposition, the surface of the products was repeatedly rinsed using deionized water and anhydrous ethanol to obtain NiCoP.

nodes.description: HER performance in 1.0 M KOH alkaline electrolyte
nodes.source_text: The catalytic activities of CP, NiCoP, NiCoP-300, NiCoP-600, and Pt/C were compared. Fig. 4b shows that the overpotential values of NiCoP were 102, 142, and 166 mV at current densities of 10, 50, and 100 mAcm⁻², respectively. The Tafel slope of NiCoP was 77 mV dec⁻¹. The ECSA values of NiCoP were 41.3 cm².

nodes.description: HER performance in 1.0 M KOH alkaline electrolyte
nodes.source_text: The overpotential values of NiCoP-300 were 66, 109, and 127 mV at current densities of 10, 50, and 100 mAcm⁻², respectively. The Tafel slope of NiCoP-300 was 65 mV dec⁻¹. The ECSA values of NiCoP-300 were 123.3 cm².

nodes.description: HER performance in 1.0 M KOH alkaline electrolyte
nodes.source_text: The overpotential values of NiCoP-600 were only 48, 81, and 92 mV at current densities of 10, 50, and 100 mAcm⁻², respectively. The overpotential of NiCoP-600 was only 232 mV when the current density was 500 mA cm⁻². The Tafel slope of NiCoP-600 was only 54 mV dec⁻¹. The ECSA values of NiCoP-600 were 198.5 cm².

nodes.description: HER performance in 0.5 M H₂SO₄ acidic electrolyte
nodes.source_text: The linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves of NiCoP-600 in 0.5 M H₂SO₄ was tested. When the current density was 10 and 100 mA cm⁻², the overpotential of NiCoP-600 increased by 68.8% (112–34 mV) and 47.7% (214–112 mV), respectively, compared with that of NiCoP.

nodes.source_text: NiCoP-600 worked continuously for 24 h at a current density of 500 mA cm⁻² in 1 M KOH, and its overpotential retention rate was as high as 95.2%.

nodes.description: Cyclic voltammetry stability testing in 1.0 M KOH for 2000 cycles
nodes.source_text: In addition to the i-t test, the LSV curve of NiCoP-600 at 0.8 - 1.4 V for 2000 cycles was also tested. The results showed that the overpotential of the LSV curve decreased by only 2 mV at a current density of 100 mA cm⁻² after 2000 cycles, and the potential retention rate was as high as 97.9%.

nodes.description: OER performance in 1.0 M KOH alkaline electrolyte
nodes.source_text: Furthermore, the OER of NiCoP and NiCoP-600 were also measured in alkaline solution. As shown in Fig. 6a, the activity of NiCoP-600 increased by 13% compared with that of NiCoP at a current density of 100 mAcm⁻².

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in 1.0 M KOH with NiCoP-600 as both cathode and anode
nodes.source_text: The LSV results show that NiCoP-600||NiCoP-600 outperformed Pt/C||RuO₂ at current densities greater than 54 mAcm⁻². The results show that 62 and 32 mL of H₂ and O₂ accumulated in the measuring cylinder, respectively, after 24 min, and the ratio was close to 2:1, which confirms that the Faradaic efficiency of NiCoP-600 was close to 100%. Fig. 6d shows that the NiCoP-600||NiCoP-600 couple can be maintained stably for 24 h at a current density of 100 mA cm⁻², with a potential retention of up to 98.7%.

nodes.characterization_summary: Energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy confirms uniform distribution of Ni, Co, and P elements on the surface of NiCoP-600, confirming successful preparation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1j-m show the energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy results for NiCoP-600. The elements Ni, Co, and P were uniformly distributed on the surface, which also confirmed the successful preparation of NiCoP.

nodes.characterization_summary: Selected area electron diffraction shows polycrystalline properties of NiCoP-600, with crystal orientation matching the HRTEM observations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SAED in Fig. 1i shows the polycrystalline properties of NiCoP-600, which matched the crystal orientation of NiCoP in the HRTEM.

nodes.characterization_summary: Brunauer-Emmett-Teller analysis shows specific surface areas of 1.39 m²/g for CP, 3.75 m²/g for NiCoP, and 4.73 m²/g for NiCoP-600, indicating increased surface area with magnetic field application.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. S3 shows the adsorption-desorption isotherms for CP, NiCoP, and NiCoP-600 with specific surface areas of 1.39, 3.75, and 4.73 m²/g, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show diffraction peaks at 40.9°, 44.8°, 47.5°, and 75.4° corresponding to (111), (201), (210), and (212) crystal planes of NiCoP (PDF # 71-2336), with peaks at 26.3° and 54.5° attributed to (002) and (004) planes of carbon.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3a shows XRD patterns of CP, NiCoP, and NiCoP-600. For NiCoP and NiCoP-600 samples, a series of diffraction peaks at 40.9°, 44.8°, 47.5°, and 75.4° correspond to the (111), (201), (210), and (212) crystal planes of NiCoP (PDF # 71-2336)

nodes.characterization_summary: Vibrating sample magnetometer measurements show that the magnetic properties of NiCoP-600 were improved compared with those of NiCoP, with hysteresis loops indicating enhanced magnetization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The magnetic properties of NiCoP and NiCoP-600 were measured with a VSM, and the hysteresis loops are shown in Fig. 3b. The results show that the magnetic properties of NiCoP-600 were improved compared with those of NiCoP (Table S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS analysis reveals Ni 2p peaks with Ni-P bonds at 870.1 and 852.9 eV, Ni-O bonds at 873.9 and 856.2 eV, and satellite peaks at 880.4 and 861.9 eV. Co 2p shows Co-P bonds at 793.3 and 778.3 eV, Co-O bonds at 796.9 and 781.2 eV, and satellite peaks at 803.4 and 785.1 eV. P 2p shows P-M bond at 129.6 eV and P-O bond at 133.1 eV. NiCoP-600 shows positive shifts in Ni-P and Co-P binding energies (0.3-0.5 eV) and negative shift in P-M bond (-0.2 eV) compared to NiCoP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3d, the high-resolution spectrum of NiCoP-600 Ni 2p consisted of three pairs of bimodal peaks. The weak peaks at 870.1 and 852.9 eV are attributed to the Ni-P bond... the Ni-P bond of Ni 2p₁/₂ and Ni 2p₃/₂ orbitals positively shifted by 0.3 and 0.4 eV, respectively, the Co-P bond of Co 2p₁/₂ and Co 2p₃/₂ orbitals positively shifted by more than 0.5 eV, and the P-M bond of P 2p negatively shifted by 0.2 eV.

properties.description: Energy shift between NiCoP and NiCoP-600

nodes.characterization_summary: Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry determined element contents: NiCoP contains 24.5 wt% Ni, 32.6 wt% Co, and 2.1 wt% P; NiCoP-600 contains 19.9 wt% Ni, 36.2 wt% Co, and 2.2 wt% P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) was used to test the element contents in NiCoP and NiCoP-600. The results are shown in Table S3, and the contents of Ni, Co, and P in NiCoP were 24.5%, 32.6%, and 2.1%, respectively. However, the weight percentage of Ni in NiCoP-600 was lower than that of NiCoP at 19.9%; the weight percentage of Co was higher than that of NiCoP at 36.2% and the content of P was 2.2%.

nodes.characterization_summary: Linear sweep voltammetry in 1.0 M KOH shows NiCoP-600 has overpotentials of 48 mV at 10 mA/cm², 81 mV at 50 mA/cm², and 92 mV at 100 mA/cm², significantly lower than NiCoP (102, 142, 166 mV) and NiCoP-300 (66, 109, 127 mV). In 0.5 M H₂SO₄, NiCoP-600 shows overpotentials of 34 mV at 10 mA/cm² and 112 mV at 100 mA/cm².
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 4b shows that the overpotential values of NiCoP-600 were only 48, 81, and 92 mV at current densities of 10, 50, and 100 mAcm⁻², respectively, and were much lower than that of NiCoP (102, 142, and 166 mV) and NiCoP-300 (66, 109, and 127 mV)... When the current density was 10 and 100 mA cm⁻², the overpotential of NiCoP-600 increased by 68.8% (112–34 mV) and 47.7% (214–112 mV), respectively, compared with that of NiCoP.

nodes.characterization_summary: Tafel slope analysis shows NiCoP-600 has a Tafel slope of 54 mV/dec in 1.0 M KOH, smaller than NiCoP (77 mV/dec) and NiCoP-300 (65 mV/dec), indicating faster reaction kinetics following the Volmer-Heyrovsky mechanism.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, the Tafel slope of NiCoP-600 was only 54 mVdec⁻¹ (Fig. 4c), which is smaller than that of NiCoP (77 mV dec⁻¹) and NiCoP-300 (65 mVdec⁻¹), implying that NiCoP-600 has faster reaction kinetics and that the HER process follows the Volmer-Heyrovsky mechanism.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cyclic voltammetry at sweep rates of 20-200 mV/s was used to measure double-layer capacitance (Cdl) and electrochemical active surface area (ECSA). NiCoP, NiCoP-300, and NiCoP-600 show ECSA values of 41.3, 123.3, and 198.5 cm², respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Double-layer capacitance (Cdl) and electrochemical active surface area (ECSA) measurements were used to determine the number of active sites. As shown in Fig. 4d and S33, the ECSA values of NiCoP, NiCoP-300, and NiCoP-600 were 41.3, 123.3, and 198.5 cm², respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy Nyquist plots show NiCoP-600 has the smallest charge transfer impedance compared to NiCoP and NiCoP-300, indicating the dense braided rope structure and Co-rich Ni/Co ratio jointly promote charge transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, the Nyquist diagrams for NiCoP, NiCoP-300, and NiCoP-600 are shown in Fig. 4e. Notably, NiCoP-600 had the smallest charge transfer impedance, which means that the dense braided rope structure and Co-rich Ni/Co ratio jointly promote the charge transfer

nodes.characterization_summary: Chronopotentiometry at 10 mA/cm² for 24 hours shows NiCoP-600 maintains an overpotential retention rate of 98.6% and 98.2%. At 500 mA/cm² for 24 hours, the retention rate is 95.2%. After 2000 cyclic voltammetry cycles, the overpotential decreases by only 2 mV at 100 mA/cm² with a potential retention rate of 97.9%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 4f-S35, NiCoP-600 was operated continuously for 24 h at a current density of 10 mAcm⁻², and its overpotential retention rate was as high as 98.6% and 98.2%... NiCoP-600 worked continuously for 24 h at a current density of 500 mA cm⁻² in 1 M KOH, and its overpotential retention rate was as high as 95.2% (Fig. S36)... the overpotential of the LSV curve decreased by only 2 mV at a current density of 100 mA cm⁻² after 2000 cycles, and the potential retention rate was as high as 97.9%.

nodes.characterization_summary: Water contact angle measurements show CP at 134.1°, NiCoP at 125.2°, NiCoP-300 at 114.7°, and NiCoP-600 at 101.6°, indicating improved wettability with magnetic field application.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2d and S21 show the water contact angles of CP, NiCoP, NiCoP-300, and NiCoP-600, which were 134.1°, 125.2°, 114.7°, and 101.6°, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-speed camera observations at 1000 fps show bubble coverage on catalyst surface without magnetic field was 20.3% with average bubble size of 52 μm, while with 600 mT magnetic field, coverage decreased to 5.6% and average bubble size decreased to 30 μm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. S23 shows the bubbles on the catalyst surface with and without a magnetic field. The results clearly show that the coverage rate of bubbles on the catalyst surface was as high as 20.3% without a magnetic field, and the average bubble size was 52 μm (Fig. S24). Remarkably, when a 600 mT magnetic field was applied, the bubble coverage rate on the catalyst surface decreased to 5.6% and the average bubble size decreased to 30 μm (Fig. S25)

nodes.characterization_summary: Turnover frequency at 100 mV overpotential shows NiCoP-600 has a TOF of 2.5 × 10⁻² s⁻¹, which is 36 times higher than NiCoP (6.9 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹) and 12 times higher than NiCoP-300 (2.1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹).
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiCoP-600 exhibited a significant TOF of 2.5 × 10⁻² s⁻¹ at a potential of 100 mV (Fig. S32), 36 times higher than NiCoP (6.9 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹) and 12 times higher than NiCoP-300 (2.1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: Density functional theory calculations show NiCoP (201) surface has hydrogen adsorption-free energy (ΔGH*) of -0.25 eV, lower than Ni-P (-0.59 eV) and Co-P (-1.01 eV), indicating superior synergistic effect of Ni/Co. The d-band center of NiCoP (-1.52 eV) is farther from the Fermi level than Ni-P (-1.46 eV) or Co-P (-1.37 eV), facilitating H* desorption.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 5b, the ΔGH* value of NiCoP is -0.25 eV, which is lower than that of Ni-P (-0.59 eV) and Co-P (-1.01 eV), indicating that the synergistic effect of Ni/Co is superior to the H* adsorption kinetics of Ni or Co at a single active site... the d-band center of NiCoP (-1.52 eV) is farther from the Fermi level than that of Ni-P (-1.46 eV) or Co-P (-1.37 eV).
